sheets.title: Settings › Security › Duress, off — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: A sealed password vault, Settings › Security scrolled to Duress. The base build has no Duress row: the only duress panel sat behind a mode switch that is off on every deployment. On the branch it is one read-only row with one Add key, drawn the way every unlock method is.
sheets.after: #duress-profiles 358x162 @16,71; Security rows 14; row reads 'Duress code · 8 to 12 digits. Not one you unlock with.'

sheets.title: The ceremony: choose what it shows, type it twice, say you understand — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Add opens one sheet. Two outcomes only, the two the unlock path applies: an empty decoy vault, or the refusal a wrong password gets. The commit key stays disabled until the code is 8 to 12 digits, matches, and the acknowledgement is ticked. The base has no such sheet, so its capture is the same Security page.
sheets.after: dialog 'Duress code': outcome switch, two code fields, one acknowledgement, one commit key

sheets.title: Turned on — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: After Turn on duress code. The code is sealed, proven to open its slot, and armed against the vault that is open; the sheet closes and the row says what is set. Change replaces it; Remove is beside it inside the sheet.
sheets.after: row reads 'Duress code ✓ · Set on this device. What it does is sealed with it.'; key is Change
